findings.claim: README: 'DAI: supply invariant, with permit'. status.json sequences: 'Seq.lean 10 (top-level messages and finite sequences, without permit) + PermitSeq.lean 13 (with permit: ... process_step_all, inv_callsP)'.
findings.what_is_actually_proved: An inductive step for ONE run of EthLib's processMessage with its default meter, plus a linear chain model. process_step_all: for a message with message.code = CODE, no precompile target, data below 2^256 bytes, Paris <= fork < Glamsterdam, NoDelegation1 of the start state and Sep (callKeys message), a run 'processMessage fork message state substate = .ok ended' is a GoodCall, a PermitCall or an Untouched step. inv_callsP: Inv is kept along a CallsP chain. Everything that is not such a run is the constructor 'other', whose only content is the ASSUMPTION Untouched C S S' (every storage word of C kept). It is proved only for a failed processMessage (untouched_process_failed). Not proved, and so outside the theorem: (a) any link to a transaction or a block: no file of DaiVerify or TokenKit mentions processMessageCall, processTransaction or prepareFirstFrame. EthLib's transaction layer does not call processMessage with the default meter: it passes first.meter and first.held and a message whose code it read from the state (Process.lean:300-312, 336-337). Upstream usdt-verify proves that link (Summary.lean:549, Usdt/Invariant/SeqMeter.lean); it was not ported. (b) message.code = CODE is a hypothesis on the message; nothing ties the code stored for C in the state to CODE, before or after a step. (c) Calls made by other contracts into DAI. A successful nested run is a GoodCall by its definition (any bound, any depth), and processRunner calls processMessage with the default meter, so process_step_all does apply to the child message taken alone. But the chain cannot express what the outer frames do next: a later revert of an outer frame restores an OLDER storage of C, which is neither Untouched nor a GoodCall from the current state. The invariant still holds there (the older state had it), but no theorem says so. (d) No base case: Inv is not shown for any state (constructor not analysed, no chain state). In practice mint and burn of DAI are reached through other contracts (the wards are contracts such as DaiJoin: from memory, not checked live), so the supply changing calls on mainnet are of kind (c). The file header of Seq.lean and the status file say 'top-level' and 'assumption of the step', so this is disclosed; the README headline is wider than the theorem.

findings.claim: supply_<fn> for 21 functions, supply_preserved, supply_permit, and the 10 write readable theorems hold 'under Sep (callKeys message) (assumed, not proved)'.
findings.what_is_actually_proved: True as stated, and disclosed. Sep is local to one call: for the 3 key words (caller, first two arguments masked to 160 bits) it asks that slot 1 is no balance slot, each balance slot is unique among the 2^160 address words, and the allowance, wards and nonces slots of these keys are no balance slot, not slot 1, and (allowance against nonces) differ. It is not the false global form. It cannot be proved in Lean (2^160 keccak values), and Sep.total is needed even for an empty key list, so no supply_ theorem and no hsep readable theorem has a closed machine-checked instance. In a chain each call carries its own Sep inside GoodCall / PermitCall, so inv_callsP is over chains whose every call met it. The keys cover every slot the code hashes: transferFrom, pull, move, burn use allowance[arg1][caller]; permit uses nonces[arg1] and allowance[arg1][arg2] (checked against the statements of burn_readable, transferFrom_readable, permit_readable).

findings.claim: status.json assumptions: 'path specs, ok_, supply, readable from Berlin; Seq from Paris; permit from Paris and before Glamsterdam. One-counter gas meter (Nat)'.
findings.what_is_actually_proved: As stated, with one consequence that is easy to miss. Every theorem is over 'Evm fork Nat'. EthLib runs transactions with the Nat meter only before Glamsterdam: processTransaction uses StateGasMeter from Glamsterdam (Process.lean:438). So GoodCall, goodCall_process and process_step, which only ask .berlin <= fork or .paris <= fork, are for Glamsterdam and later about a meter the transaction layer does not use. The effective range of every sequence result is Paris <= fork < Glamsterdam (Paris, Shanghai, Cancun, Prague, Osaka, BPO1 to BPO5), and of every frame result Berlin to BPO5. The bytes were read at block 26386793 (2026-11-10). If mainnet had activated Glamsterdam by then, no sequence or permit theorem covers the fork that is live; I could not check which fork that block is on.

findings.claim: CODE is the deployed bytecode; 22 selectors; supply_preserved and the dispatcher cover every function.
findings.what_is_actually_proved: Holds. CODE_NAT / CODE_SIZE equal survey/tokens/DAI/runtime.hex byte for byte (7904 bytes; keccak 4e36f96e...1ac7 as in Test/Hash.lean and SOURCE.md; data/dai.runtime.hex is the same file). The bytes hold exactly 22 'DUP1 PUSH4 k EQ PUSH2 d JUMPI' entries, equal to ENTRIES of Map.lean in order, every destination a JUMPDEST, and the 22 keys are exactly keccak(signature)[:4] of the 22 functions of abi.json; no other PUSH4 constant exists. ends_ok_dispatch: a run from pc 0 that ends with no error has >= 4 bytes of data, value 0 and the key of an entry (the three fallbacks are proved to end in an error for every gas). supply_preserved matches on all 22 entries; 21 go to supply_<fn>, the permit entry is closed by the hypothesis 'selector message.data ≠ 0x8fcbaf0c' and is added back by supply_permit and process_step_all. Static frames and a missing account are handled: ok_<fn> of every writer derives message.isStatic = false and hasAccount from the run (the other case is a proved stuck path).

findings.claim: status.json contract_findings (who can mint, burn, permit rules).
findings.what_is_actually_proved: The readable theorems I read support them, each as 'a run that ends with no error implies ...' (necessary conditions and exact effects; sufficiency is only shown by the witnesses). Worth telling the owner: (1) mint_readable: the only checks are wards[caller] = 1 and no overflow of balanceOf[usr] and totalSupply; no cap, no zero address check. rely_readable: any ward can make any address a ward; deny likewise removes any ward, itself included. There is no theorem at sequence level about who the wards are or can become; that is live state. (2) burn_readable: no ward needed; caller = usr, or allowance[usr][caller] >= wad (the largest word is not reduced). (3) permit_readable: the digest uses the word of storage slot 5 as domain separator; the bytes have no CHAINID opcode, so the separator is fixed at construction and a signature is valid on any chain fork that shares this storage. Allowance is set to 0 or to the largest word only. expiry = 0 means no expiry. The nonce sum is unchecked (wraps at 2^256, not reachable in practice). v is cut to its low byte. Only ECRECOVER is used: a contract holder cannot permit. (4) transferFrom, pull, move, burn skip the allowance when caller = src and never reduce an allowance equal to the largest word. (5) Every function reverts on value; a nonzero value at top level is proved to fail (process_value_fails).
